5ee4188f2a.substituent_description: The central benzene ring (drawn with a circle) is 1,2,3-trisubstituted: NH on the lower-right vertex (C1), an O-CH2-CH3 group on the bottom vertex (C2, ortho to the NH), and a 4-methyl triazole ring (5-membered ring containing three N, one of them bearing CH3) on the lower-left vertex (C3, ortho to the ethoxy and meta to the NH), joined through the triazole carbon that sits between the N-CH3 and a ring N. The NH is bonded directly to a ring N (N-N bond) in the left, partly saturated ring of a fused 6/6 bicycle; the right ring of the bicycle (circle) contains a second ring N, has CH3 on the carbon next to that N, and on the carbon on the other side of that N carries an N-linked 4-membered ring (azetidine N) bearing two CH3 on the carbon next to N and CH3O on the next carbon.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The left ring of the fused bicycle has one double bond drawn on the bond leading to a fusion carbon of the circled ring
NH is joined directly to a ring N (N-N link)
Triazole is drawn with Kekule double bonds while the benzene and the circled bicycle ring use circles
5ee4188f2a.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white. Triazole has 2 double bonds, the left bicycle ring has 1; circles are not counted as double bonds. The ethoxy is drawn as O, CH2 (with a bond down) and CH3.

988abb63de.substituent_description: A 3,4-difluorophenyl ring (F on the meta and para positions relative to the ring carbon bearing NH) is attached through NH to an amide C(=O), which connects to a stereocentre CH carrying a hashed-bond methyl and an ester O. That O is acylated by C(=O)-CH2-CH2- whose end is bonded to the N of a 2H-1,4-benzoxazin-3-one (benzene fused to a 6-membered ring containing O and N; the carbon next to N is C=O and the CH2 sits between that C=O and the ring O).
988abb63de.notes: Typeset structure. Double bonds: 3 in difluorophenyl, 3 in the benzo ring, 3 C=O (amide, ester, lactam). The methyl on the stereocentre is a plain hashed-bond line with no label. No written stereo descriptors.

c252ca16c1.substituent_description: A long zigzag unbranched chain (about 11 vertex carbons between Et and NH, exact count uncertain) starts at Et and ends at NH-C(=O)- on a benzene ring (circle). That benzene is para-disubstituted: the amide carbonyl at one vertex and a CH2CH2 (two-carbon) linker at the opposite vertex going to C4 of a piperidine ring (6-membered, one N). The piperidine N is acylated as a urea N-C(=O)-NH- joined to a second benzene (circle) which carries N(Me)2 para to the NH.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Number of carbons in the long zigzag chain is hard to count exactly (about 11 vertices)
c252ca16c1.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white; thin line, small dots at some vertices. Double bonds are the two C=O (amide and urea). The N of NMe2 has two separate Me labels.

1556a913f3.substituent_description: A carbazole-type tricycle (benzene circle, 5-membered ring with N, benzene circle) has Et on the ring N, and a CH2 on the right-hand benzene ring that links to the N of a 6-membered N-ring (piperidine). The carbon opposite that N in the piperidine is a spiro carbon shared with a 5-membered ring fused to a third benzene ring (circle); in the five-membered ring the carbon next to the spiro carbon bears OH on a solid bold wedge, and the next carbon (attached to the benzene) bears NHAc on a hashed bond.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Small stray dot on the left edge of the piperidine ring could be read as an extra vertex (ring read as 6-membered)
H of NHAc has a crossbar that makes it look like N+HAc
1556a913f3.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white. No explicit double bonds; all aromatic rings drawn as circles, the N-containing five-ring has no double bonds. One solid wedge (OH) and one hashed bond (NHAc).

015d4074cd.substituent_description: A benzene ring bears EtOOC on one vertex and, at the para vertex, a CH=C(CH3)- unit (the C=C double bond is drawn, with a plain methyl line on the carbon attached to the second aryl). That second aryl is the aromatic ring of a tetrahydronaphthalene fused to a saturated 6-membered ring that has two quaternary carbons, each bearing two methyl lines (four methyls in total); the vinyl carbon is attached to the aromatic carbon adjacent to the CH that sits next to a ring-fusion carbon (position 2 of the 5,5,8,8-tetramethyl-5,6,7,8-tetrahydronaphthalene).
015d4074cd.notes: Typeset structure. Double bonds: 3 in the phenyl, 3 in the tetralin aromatic ring, 1 C=C. All methyls are unlabeled plain lines. No stereo descriptors written.

62d62d3a8a.substituent_description: A chain reads H2N-C(=O)-NH-CH2CH2CH2- to a stereocentre (solid wedge to the chain) that carries C(=O)NH-aryl and an NH which acylates the next residue: a CH with iPr on a solid wedge and NHBoc, then C(=O)-NH. The aryl is a benzene with the amide NH at one vertex, CH2OH at the para vertex, and CH2-N(Me)-C(=O)-O-CH2- at the position ortho to the CH2OH and meta to the NH; the carbamate O-CH2 is attached to C9 of a fluorene (two benzene rings joined through a five-membered ring, the C9 carbon being sp3 CH).
62d62d3a8a.notes: Typeset structure. Double bonds: 4 C=O (urea, two amides, carbamate) and 3 in each of three benzene rings. Two solid wedges (iPr carbon and the CH2 side chain of the other stereocentre). No stereo descriptors written.

8b3fbdaaf8.substituent_description: A quinoline (ring N at position 1) carries an NH-aryl substituent on C2 (the carbon next to N) and a C(=O)NHBn carboxamide on C4. The aryl on the NH is a benzene ring with a Me on the carbon ortho to the carbon bearing NH.
8b3fbdaaf8.notes: Typeset structure. Double bonds: 5 in the quinoline, 3 in the tolyl ring, 1 C=O.

64cc25c179.substituent_description: A piperidine (6-ring with N) has EtO on a solid wedge on C4 (counting N as 1 and going through the carbon next to the aryl-bearing carbon: N1, C2 bears aryl on a hashed bond, C3 CH2, C4 bears EtO), and the ring N is attached through a CH2 to C4 of an indole. The aryl on piperidine C2 is a benzene (circle) bearing, relative to the piperidine attachment at C1, an O-CH2-CH2-NHAc chain at C2 (ortho) and HO2C at C4 (para). The indole (benzene circle fused to a pyrrole ring with NH and a C=C double bond) has the CH2N at C4, MeO at C5 (adjacent to C4) and an unlabeled methyl line at C7.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Methyl at the right of the indole is only a short unlabeled line
Stray tick mark beside the piperidine N label
Indole is drawn with a circle in the six-ring but a Kekule C=C in the five-ring
64cc25c179.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white. One double bond (indole C2=C3). One solid wedge (EtO) and one hashed bond (to the aryl). No written stereo descriptors.

76aca7380e.substituent_description: An indole (benzene circle fused to a pyrrole ring with a C=C) has Ac on the pyrrole carbon C3, and the indole N is alkylated with CH2-C(=O)-N(iPr)-CH2-C(=O)-NH-CH2-aryl. The aryl is a benzene (circle) with the CH2 at C1, F at C2 (ortho) and Cl at C3 (meta). A CH2-C(=O)- chain from the benzo ring carbon next to the indole N-bearing carbon (C7) leads to the N of a piperidine whose carbon beta to N (position 3) carries two F atoms.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The photo is cropped at the right edge: the indole benzo ring is cut off with a short stub at its right vertex, so any substituent there cannot be seen
iPr label is small and smudged
Image is rotated and has perspective distortion
76aca7380e.notes: Handwritten, black ink on grey paper photo. Double bonds: 3 C=O and 1 indole C=C. Benzene rings drawn as circles.
